- Represent each physical concern (transit, turn, productivity, battery feasibility) exactly once; fold turn angle into an effective approach distance and reuse that single term for transit and budgeting rather than adding separate turn penalties.
- Derive one shared dimensionless battery margin (budget minus leg cost minus depot-return cost, normalised by budget) and reuse it for both low-energy urgency and feasibility, so signals stay coupled rather than double-counted.
- Normalise distances, lengths and transit costs by batch statistics (e.g. batch mean) so selectivity is scale-free across fields; let low-battery urgency scale transit sensitivity as the only place low-energy pressure enters.

    eps = 1e-9
    frac = float(np.clip(energy_left_frac, 0.0, 1.0))
    dist = np.nan_to_num(np.asarray(dist_m, dtype=float), nan=1e6, posinf=1e6)
    length = np.nan_to_num(np.asarray(swath_len_m, dtype=float), nan=0.0, posinf=1e6)
    depot = np.nan_to_num(np.asarray(depot_dist_m, dtype=float), nan=1e6, posinf=1e6)
    turn = np.nan_to_num(np.asarray(turn_deg, dtype=float), nan=0.0) % 360.0
    fits_arr = np.clip(np.nan_to_num(np.asarray(fits, dtype=float), nan=0.0), 0.0, 1.0)

    # turn-adjusted approach cost, normalised by candidate-set mean (dimensionless)
